And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.

blocks.html: But the centurion ignored Paul's warning.
A storm at sea

items.html: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.
But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.

blocks.html: After sailing by Crete, a strong wind began to blow.

items.html: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.
And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.

blocks.html:
So we took down the sails,

and were driven before the wind.

items.html: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;

blocks.html:
On the second day of the storm,

we lightened the ship by throwing some cargo overboard.

items.html: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.

blocks.html: The next day, we gave up all hope.

items.html: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.

blocks.html:
Then Paul stood up and said,

If you had listened to me, we would have stayed in Crete, and we'd be all be safe now.

items.html: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship.

blocks.html:
But don't worry.

We'll survive, but the ship won't.

items.html: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,

blocks.html: Because last night an angel of God stood by me, and said,

items.html: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

blocks.html:
Don't be afraid, Paul.

You'll have a trial with Caesar.

And God has given you those who sail with you.

items.html: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.

blocks.html:
So we'll be OK.

But first we'll be shipwrecked on an island.

items.html: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;
And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.
Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

blocks.html: On the 14th night, the crew feared we might hit some rocks, so they cast out four anchors.

items.html: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,
Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.

blocks.html:
The crew were about to abandon ship,

when Paul said to the centurion,

If they leave the ship, we will all die.

items.html: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

blocks.html: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat, and everyone stayed on board.

items.html: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.
Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.

blocks.html:
Paul said to everyone,

You need to eat.

You haven't eaten anything in 14 days.

items.html: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.

blocks.html: So they all cheered up and ate.

items.html: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.

blocks.html: There were a total of 276 people on board.
The shipwreck

items.html: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.

blocks.html: After they ate, they raised the anchors, hoisted the mainsail, and sailed toward shore.

items.html: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.

blocks.html: The ship ran aground and was destroyed.

items.html: And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

blocks.html:
The soldiers wanted to kill all the prisoners,

to prevent them from escaping by swimming away.

items.html: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:

blocks.html:
But the centurion wanted to save Paul's life,

so he let them swim to land.

items.html: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.

blocks.html:
Those who couldn't swim came to shore on pieces of the ship.

Everyone made it safely to land.
On the island of Malta

items.html: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.

blocks.html:
When they got to shore,

they knew the island was called Melita (Malta).

items.html: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

blocks.html:
The barbarous natives were kind to us,

kindling a fire to protect us from the rain and cold.

items.html: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

blocks.html:
But Paul was bitten by a snake [1]

when he was gathering firewood.

items.html: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.

blocks.html:
When the barbarians saw the venomous beast hanging from his hand, they said to themselves,

This man is a murderer.

He survived the sea, but now he will die.

items.html: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.

blocks.html: Paul shook the beast off into the fire, and was unhurt.

items.html: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

blocks.html:
Since he didn't die, they changed their minds,

and said he was a god.

items.html: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.

blocks.html: The governor of the island was a man named Publius, who gave us a place to stay for three days.

items.html: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.

blocks.html:
His father was sick with a fever.

But Paul healed him by praying and laying his hands on him.

items.html: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:
Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.

blocks.html: Others with diseases came, and Paul healed them too.
From Malta to Rome

items.html: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.
And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.

blocks.html: After three months, we sailed from Malta to Syracuse.

items.html: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:

blocks.html:
We stayed three days in Syracuse,

and then sailed to Rhegium and Puteoli,

items.html: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.
And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.

blocks.html: and finally, Rome.
Paul in Rome

items.html: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.

blocks.html:
When we arrived in Rome,

Paul was kept alone under a soldier's watch.

items.html: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.

blocks.html:
After three days, Paul called the Jewish leaders, and said to them,

I've done nothing wrong,

yet I was imprisoned by the Romans in Jerusalem.

items.html: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.
But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.

blocks.html:
They would have let me go,

but the Jews wouldn't let them.

So I appealed to Caesar.

items.html: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judea concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.
But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.

blocks.html:
The Jewish leaders said to Paul,

We haven't heard anything about that from Judea.

But we'd like to hear from you about this sect,

since everyone speaks against it.

items.html: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.

blocks.html: So many came to visit Paul, where he talked all day about God, Jesus, the law of Moses, and the prophets.

items.html: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.

blocks.html: Some of them believed him, and some didn't.

items.html: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Isaiah the prophet unto our fathers,
Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:

blocks.html:
When they couldn't come to an agreement, they started to leave.

But then Paul began to speak, saying,

The Holy Ghost said it well through Isaiah, who said,

They'll hear but they won't understand.

They'll see but they won't perceive.

items.html: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.

blocks.html:
Because their hearts are gross, their ears are dull, and their eyes are closed.

So they won't see with their eyes, hear with their ears, or understand with their hearts.

So they won't be converted and I won't heal them.

items.html: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.

blocks.html:
Therefore, God's salvation is sent to the Gentiles, [2]

and they will hear it.

items.html: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.

blocks.html: After he said these things, the Jews left.

items.html: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,

blocks.html: And Paul lived in a rented house for two years,

items.html: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.

blocks.html: preaching to everyone and no one could stop him.

footnotes.html:
When Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand. (v.3)

Paul is bitten by a poisonous snake and yet lives. The "barbarians" who were shipwrecked with him thought he must be a murderer since he was bitten; but then they changed their minds and thought him to be a god since he didn't die. (The snake story is especially interesting since there are no poisonous snakes on Malta, and there is no evidence of their existence in the past.)

The salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles. (v.28)

Should the gospel be preached to everyone?
